title: Find the cause of system alerts and open a fix
summary: A developer's team had Claude Code routines hunt down why alerts fired, explain it in Slack and propose fixes; they say their first urgent alert reached a merged fix in 13 minutes.
agent_role: The agent investigates the alert, finds the cause, posts an explanation in Slack and opens a proposed code fix; humans review and merge.
outcome: Author reports their first top-priority incident went from alert to merged fix in 13 minutes.
what_they_did: A developer's team set up scheduled Claude routines to watch for incident alerts. When one fires, the agent hunts for the root cause. It explains the cause in Slack and opens a proposed code fix for review.
how_it_went: The author says their first top-priority incident went from alert to merged fix in 13 minutes.
worth_knowing: The author's point is that finding the cause, not writing the fix, is now the slow part of bug fixing.
prompt: When an alert arrives from [alerting tool] for [repo URL], investigate it. Read recent logs, errors and code changes to find the most likely root cause. Post a plain-language summary in [Slack channel]: what broke, why, and how confident you are. Then prepare a fix on a new branch and open it as a draft for review. Do not merge or deploy anything; wait for a person to approve.

curation.rationale: Genuine incident-response agent with a concrete 13-minute result, but the post is very thin and details sit in a linked article not provided.
